bins.name: Blue cart

bins.name: Black cart

bins.name: Drop-off
bins.accepts: Food scraps, yard waste, batteries, e-waste, chemicals, textiles

snack_wrapper.why: The City asks residents to keep bags and other soft plastics out of the Blue Cart.

foam.why: Foam is #6 plastic, which the City does not recycle because there is no market for it.

prep: No prep
plastic_utensil_straw.why: The Blue Cart takes plastic bottles and containers; utensils and straws are not on the City's list.

prep: Put it in loose, not in a bag

paper.why: Newspaper, magazines, junk mail and office paper are accepted.

Wet or food-soiled bags go in the black cart
paper_bag.why: Paper bags are listed with the paper the City accepts.

prep: Break the box down and flatten it
Put it in loose, not in a bag
cardboard.why: Cardboard is accepted; flatten boxes to save space in the cart.

Grease marks are fine
pizza_box.why: The City says pizza boxes can be recycled if they are empty; food scrap drop-offs do not take them.

prep: Not in the blue cart
Not accepted at food scrap drop-offs
soiled_paper.why: Napkins and paper are not accepted at Chicago's food scrap drop-offs, and soiled paper can't be recycled.

paper_cup.why: Chicago does not list paper cups as accepted, so the black cart is the safe choice.

Don't crush it

Don't crush it

aluminum_foil.why: Aluminum foil and pie tins are listed with the metal the City accepts.

prep: Usable pots and pans: donate or reuse
metal_lid_scrap.why: The Blue Cart takes steel and aluminum cans and foil; lids and scrap metal are not on the City's list.

Take the lid off

glass_bottle_jar.why: Glass bottles and jars are accepted.

drinking_glass_ceramic.why: Only glass bottles and jars are accepted, so drinking glasses, ceramics and broken glass go in the black cart.

prep: Better: take it to a City food scrap drop-off site (sign up first, no bags of any kind)
Otherwise it goes in the black cart
food_scraps.why: Chicago has no curbside compost cart, so food scraps are garbage unless you use the free City drop-off sites, which take all food, including meat and bones.

prep: Bag it separately from garbage and recycling
Call 311 to request a pickup
Christmas trees: use the City's January tree drop-off
yard_waste.why: The City collects bagged yard waste separately on request and composts it; it is not accepted at food scrap sites.

prep: Rechargeable, lithium and car batteries: take to the Household Chemicals & Computer Recycling Facility
Never in the blue cart
Alkaline (AA, AAA, 9V): the facility does not take them; black cart
battery.why: Lithium-ion batteries cause fires at sorting plants, so they never go in the blue cart.

prep: Take it to the Household Chemicals & Computer Recycling Facility
Only listed items are taken: computers, TVs, phones, printers, keyboards
Check hours first (Tue, Thu, first Sat)
electronics.why: Illinois law bars most electronics from the trash, so Chicago sends them to its computer recycling facility.

prep: Donate wearable items
Use a textile drop-off for the rest
Never in the blue cart
textile.why: Textiles can't be captured at the recycling plant, so the City points residents to reuse and drop-off outlets.

prep: Donate wearable pairs
Never in the blue cart
shoes.why: The City's older guide lists shoes as a donation or drop-off item, not a Blue Cart item.

prep: Make sure it is fully out
cigarette_butt.why: Butts can't be recycled; non-recyclables go in the black cart.

blister_pack.why: Mixed plastic and foil packaging is not a bottle or container the Blue Cart takes.

rope_string.why: Hoses, cords and other tanglers jam sorting machines at the recycling plant.

squeezable_tube.why: Tubes are not bottles or containers the Blue Cart takes.
